title: Buildings that changed hands shortly before the public bought them
question: Did the seller buy the building only a short time before selling it to the City, and for how much less?
finding: 4 finished buildings had last changed hands within four years of the public purchase, 3 of them within two. The clearest case: 681-687 Ellis Street last changed hands in 2021-06, was carried by the assessor at $14,280,000 afterwards, and was sold to the City for $19,900,000 in a file introduced in 2022-04, 39% more.
how: For each purchase, the last sale date the assessor rolls record before the City’s file. Where a roll falls between the two sales, its assessed value stands in for what the seller paid, because the assessor resets value to the sale price. Years between runs from that sale to the date the City’s file was introduced.
limits: A seller may have repaired or emptied the building, carried financing costs, or bought at a distressed price; a short holding period alone proves nothing. The assessed value can differ from the price paid (partial transfers, exclusions, appeals). Only rolls for 2019, 2022 and 2025 are on disk, so several earlier prices cannot be seen. The assessor’s roll names no owners: that the party selling to the City is the one who bought at the previous sale is an inference from there being no sale recorded in between. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
